source.title: The Heuristic Core: Understanding Subnetwork Generalization in Pretrained Language Models
source.authors: Adithya Bhaskar; Dan Friedman; Danqi Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study tests delayed out-of-domain generalization during fine-tuning of pretrained language models and examines its mechanism using pruning and effective-size measurements, rather than reproducing grokking on algorithmic datasets.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training-dynamics and subnetwork results on MNLI/HANS and QQP/PAWS-QQP. Its references to grokking on toy algorithmic tasks are cited background, not results from this study. It does not test algorithmic datasets, initialization-scale or weight-norm switches, low-norm efficiency, or optimizer/numerical-artifact explanations.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces grokking-like delayed out-of-domain (OOD) generalization while fine-tuning BERT on MNLI and QQP. It then tests whether the competing-subnetworks mechanism used to explain algorithmic grokking holds there, and finds effective size rising and a heuristic core retained rather than removed. That is a specific result that a mechanism version needs restating outside algorithmic tasks. The delayed-OOD-rise results bear on V4 and on the non-algorithmic-data part of V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that generalization is better explained by a heuristic core of shared attention heads than by competing disjoint subnetworks. These heads emerge early and compute shallow features, and later-learned heads build on them. Effective size increases with generalization. They also stress that subnetworks matching ID performance can generalize very differently.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pretrained language models on natural-language classification tasks and uses structured pruning to analyze subnetworks; it does not train small networks on small algorithmic datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that outcomes depend on subnetwork sparsity, random pruning seed, task and OOD subcase; GPT-2 results also differ between contradiction and entailment OOD cases.

fits_no_version.finding: Within a single fine-tuned model, pruned subnetworks with similar ID accuracy generalize very differently OOD (Embed-If 4.1%–50.2%). Sparser subnetworks generalize worse, with no phase transition across sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruned subnetworks of a fine-tuned LM match ID performance but vary widely in OOD generalization.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2024)
record.problems: The experiments use text-classification tasks and relatively small pretrained models; the authors caution that models with 7B+ parameters may behave differently. Some training-dynamics values are presented in figures without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional individual attention-head ablation results in Tables 3, 4, 6, and 8. Those ablations test the importance of heuristic-core heads for task accuracy rather than the delayed-generalization trajectories or effective-size predictions catalogued here.

untested.parts: No algorithmic dataset, train-vs-test trajectory, or training-set-size sweep.
No Fourier or algorithmic circuit and no continuous progress measure shown to anticipate a jump; only the effective-size / component-removal part is tested.
Initialization scale or weight-norm switching of the delay is not tested; only occurrence on text data is tested.
No pretraining dynamics; no models beyond about 125M parameters (authors caution about 7B+).
No weight decay or low-norm manipulation, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Subnetworks are pruned from one model; independently trained runs are not compared.
No optimizer or numerical controls (Adam used throughout).

missing.what: OOD accuracy over training for further HANS subcases. The delay holds for those shown; on the remaining subcases the model never gets off the ground.
Final full-model OOD accuracies giving the size of the delayed gain (e.g. SO-Swap 86.7, Embed-If 33.0, PAWS-QQP adv. 14.8).

record.verdict_notes: Changed the tranche from T2 to T5 because the main contribution is evidence against transferring the grokking mechanism account. V2 is labelled limits_scope rather than challenges because the test is in a grokking-like NLP fine-tuning setting, not the algorithmic setting where V2 is claimed. The reader's limits_scope label for V3 based on R13 is dropped: GPT-2's OOD timing is not stated, and the OOD-E decline is not a delayed-generalization measure. Rows R7–R10 and R15 are unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset, training-versus-test accuracy trajectory on such a dataset, or training-set-size sweep.
No Fourier or other algorithmic circuit on a modular-arithmetic task, and no continuous progress measure shown to anticipate an accuracy jump.
The study does not vary initialization scale or weight norm to switch delayed generalization on or off.
No LLM pretraining experiment; the tested systems are fine-tuned pretrained models, and the study cautions that much larger models such as those with 7B+ parameters may behave differently.
No test of weight decay or another low-norm bias as an efficiency mechanism, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study analyzes subnetworks within trained models, not whether independently trained networks converge to the same identifiable algorithm.
No controlled test of adaptive-optimizer instability, softmax floating-point limits, or whether controlling such factors removes delayed generalization.

rows.measure: ID and OOD accuracy over training
rows.value: In-domain accuracy saturates early; OOD accuracy starts to rise much later.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes this timing; plotted values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Delay is OOD (HANS) accuracy rising after in-domain (ID) validation accuracy saturates, not test-after-train. Full-model HANS accuracy at the end is partial on some subcases (Embed-If 33.0%, Table 3). Appendix C adds that on the other subcases the model never gets off the ground.

rows.subject: BERT (bert_base_cased, 125M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked effective subnetwork size over fine-tuning
rows.measure: Effective size, defined as the smallest faithful subnetwork size
rows.value: OOD and mixed-data generalization is accompanied by an increase in effective size.
rows.uncertainty: Accuracy values at each sparsity are averaged over three seeds.
rows.note: The authors contrast this increase with the reduction in effective size predicted by the competing-subnetworks account.
rows.check: Measures effective size over training. It increases with generalization, the opposite of the cleanup or sparsification that removal of memorizing components implies.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, effective-size analysis; Figure 6c. Faithfulness means accuracy within 3%; accuracies averaged over three pruning seeds.

rows.value: The authors report that effective size increases with generalization.

rows.subject: BERT (bert_base_cased, 125M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Counted attention-head overlap among pruned subnetworks
rows.measure: Heads shared across subnetworks and correlation between head frequencies
rows.baseline: Expected intersection of 12 random 70% sparsity subnetworks: 7.7 · 10−5 heads
rows.value: Nine attention heads appear in all subnetworks, including non-generalizing subnetworks; frequency correlation is 0.82 (p-value = 1.6 · 10−36).
rows.note: The finding is overlap rather than disjoint subnetworks.
rows.check: The heuristic heads persist in all subnetworks and appear before generalization, so they are retained, not removed. 'numbers_found 7/7' is unverifiable. The baseline is the expected random intersection (7.7e-5 heads).

source_check.locator_found: Section 4; Figures 5 and 13: nine shared heads; Spearman correlation 0.82, p = 1.6 × 10^-36; expected random intersection 7.7 × 10^-5 heads. Section 4 also verifies these heads before generalization.

rows.subject: BERT (bert_base_cased, 125M parameters)
rows.operation_detail: Counted attention-head overlap among pruned subnetworks
rows.measure: Heads shared across subnetworks and correlation between head frequencies
rows.value: Eight attention heads appear in all subnetworks; frequency correlation is 0.74 (p-value = 7.7 · 10−26).
rows.note: The study reports substantial shared-head overlap across subnetworks.
rows.check: QQP counterpart of R5. The text gives no pre-generalization checkpoint analysis for QQP, so this is weaker evidence.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V2's temporal mechanism. Eight heads occur across the final QQP subnetworks at 30% and 60% sparsity; frequency correlation is 0.74, p = 7.7 × 10^-26. No QQP pre-generalization checkpoint comparison is reported.
source_check.problem: Final-checkpoint overlap tests disjointness, but alone cannot establish reversal of V2's temporal formation-and-removal sequence.

rows.subject: BERT (bert_base_cased, 125M parameters)

rows.value: Embed-If accuracies range from 4.1% to 50.2%; subnetworks are within 2–3% of the full model on MNLI, as stated in the text.
rows.note: Different subnetworks with similar in-domain performance generalize differently.
rows.check: Variation across pruned subnetworks of one final model is not a measure of circuit formation over training, of delayed generalization, or of different training runs (V6).

rows.subject: GPT-2 small (117M)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked ID and OOD accuracy over training

conditions.value: HANS Embed-If and OOD-E entailment subcases

rows.measure: ID and OOD accuracy over training
rows.value: After 10 epochs (12270 steps), Embed-If is the only contradiction subcase with accuracy above 30%; the authors also report that OOD-E accuracy drops slightly late in training.
rows.uncertainty: Three seeds are plotted in Figure 16.
rows.note: The model generalizes poorly on the selected HANS setting, and OOD-E accuracy declines rather than improving late in training.

The authors state the model generalizes very poorly overall, and Embed-If was selected as the only subcase above 30%.
